seo.metaDescription: Which allowances run out before they reset: a strip of shaded time cells per row, with the run-out moment, the locked time and the reset.

props.markdown: Which allowances will run out before they reset. Every row is a strip of time cells shaded by the projected use, with a dot where the allowance runs out and hatching until it resets.

Use `RunwayChart` for limits that reset: API quotas, GPU hours, a usage cap per seat. Each row has its own window, a projection of cumulative use, and optionally when it runs out and when it resets. The chart shades each cell by the projected share (`breaks`, `tone`), marks the moment the allowance runs out, hatches the locked time until the reset, and draws a Now line.

To see how one allowance moved over time, use [LineChart](/docs/line-chart) with a time axis (see [time scales](/docs/time-scales)): it plots one value per moment, while the runway compares many allowances on the same dates.

Rows are built by spreading `runwayForecast` over each window: it adds the `projection`, `runsOutAt` and `resetAt`. The `now` and the windows are fixed ISO strings, so the page renders the same on every request. A row with `disconnected` is muted and has no forecast. `runwayForecast` is imported from `tally-charts/core`, whose functions a server component can call, and every prop is serializable.

`activeId` is the highlighted row, and `onActiveChange` reports hover and keyboard changes. Here both live in `useState`, so the buttons outside the chart move the highlight too, and `onSelect` with `selectedId` makes the rows a listbox. Functions and state make this a client component.

`runwayForecast` turns one window into the fields of a row. Spread the result into the row next to the `id` and `label`: `{ id, label, ...runwayForecast({ used, windowStart, resetAt, now }) }`. It returns `projection`, `runsOutAt` (only when the allowance runs out before `resetAt`), `resetAt` and the numbers `usedAtReset`, `paceRatio`, `elapsed` and `lockedMs`. The pace is the observed one unless you pass `pace`, a share per day.

A row is `{ id, label, icon?, sublabel?, projection?, runsOutAt?, resetAt?, disconnected?, status? }`. `projection` is a list of `{ at, used }` points, `used` from 0 to 1, with a straight line between the points; a row without a projection has no forecast. Cells before the first point take that point's value, so start the `domain` at `now` or include the history.

- `domain` and `now` are dates, epoch milliseconds or ISO strings. An invalid domain, or no rows, shows `empty` ("No data" by default).
- `cell` is the length of one cell: `'30m'`, `'6h'` (the default), `'1d'` or a number of milliseconds. A strip has at most 200 cells; a `cell` too short for the `domain` draws the first 200 and warns in development ("use a longer `cell`").
- `breaks` are 1 to 4 ascending level edges as shares, `[0.25, 0.5, 0.75]` by default. `n` edges make `n + 1` levels.
- `tone` (default `'neutral'`) colors the levels and the legend and is always applied: a `--ch-seq-base` set on an ancestor does not reach this chart.
- `layout` is `'auto'`, `'columns'` or `'stacked'`. `'auto'` stacks the rows when the strip would be under 240px. On the server there is no measurement, so `initialWidth` (default 960, which renders columns) decides; `labelWidth` (default 200) is the label column in pixels.
- `timeZone` is `'utc'` by default and sets the day boundaries and the dates in the status. `'local'` can differ between the server and the client.

Every cell is decided at its midpoint, in this order:

- Before the run-out, with a forecast: a level from the projection at that moment, binned by `breaks`.
- The cell that holds the run-out: the "runs out" cell, and the dot sits in it.
- After the run-out and before the reset: locked, drawn hatched.
- After the reset, or with no forecast: empty.

The cells carry that decision as `data-ch-state`: `level`, `runs-out`, `locked` or `empty` (see below). The levels use the sequential ramp `--ch-seq-1` to `--ch-seq-5`, see [Theming](/docs/theming).

The default status has two lines. The first is `Runs out <date>` when the allowance runs out, `~N% at reset` when it does not (the projected share at the reset), or `No forecast` when the row has no projection. The second is `Resets <date>`. A row with `disconnected` reads `Disconnected`.

Dates are relative to `now`:

- Within six days of `now`: weekday and time, `Fri 03:24`.
- Later in the domain: month, day and time, `Oct 21 09:21`.
- Past the end of the domain: month and day only, `Nov 9`, with ` →` after a reset.

The built-in strings ("Now", "reset", "Runs out", the legend and the table headers) are English. To change what you can, pass `status`, `legend={false}` or your own `title`. A row's own `status` wins over the `status` function, and a string from either is also the table's Status.

These names are part of the public surface (see [Stability](/docs/stability)), so you can select them with `[data-ch-part="…"]`.

- Parts: `runway`, `runway-axis`, `runway-now-label`, `runway-head-row`, `runway-rows`, `runway-row`, `runway-label`, `runway-icon`, `runway-name`, `runway-strip`, `runway-cell`, `runway-now`, `runway-reset`, `runway-reset-label`, `runway-dot`, `runway-status` and `runway-status-line`.
- `data-ch-layout`: `columns` or `stacked`.
- `data-ch-state` on a cell: `level`, `runs-out`, `locked` or `empty`.
- `data-ch-focus`: the row the keyboard cursor is on, while the listbox has focus (only with `onSelect`).
- On a row: `data-ch-active`, `data-ch-muted` (a disconnected row), `data-ch-selectable` and `data-ch-selected`.

Without `onSelect` the rows are a plain `list` of `listitem`s: there is no tab stop and no keys. With `onSelect` the rows container is a `listbox` and one tab stop. The focused row is `aria-activedescendant`, and real focus stays on the container. Tabbing in resumes at the existing cursor (set by earlier keys or a click), else at the selected row, else at the first. Hovering a row highlights it but does not move the cursor; pressing a row moves the cursor there.

`↑` and `↓` move one row, `Home` and `End` go to the first and last, and `PageUp` and `PageDown` move five. `Enter` or `Space` selects the focused row. `Esc` clears the active row, and only when one is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes. Keys with `Alt`, `Ctrl` or `Cmd` pass through. The cursor follows its row by id when `rows` change, and falls back to the first row if that row is gone.

Screen readers get a `list` (or, with `onSelect`, a `listbox`) named by `title` or `aria-labelledby` and described by `description`. Each row is announced by its label followed by its status, such as “Work account Runs out Fri 03:24 Resets Mon 09:21”; with `onSelect` each is an `option` with `aria-selected`, named from those two parts. The strips, the time axis and the legend swatches are hidden from assistive technology, and icons are hidden too. A visually hidden data table has the name, detail text, run-out, reset, projected share at reset and status of every row (`dataTable` renames it or turns it off). A custom `status` replaces the text that is read, and `null` leaves the row with its label only. A disconnected row reads “Disconnected”.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
